item.description: A projected slide now keeps its diagram pin, so both deck viewers read the source's notes and render each with the sanitizing Markdown helper.
item.label: Notes come from the diagram source

item.description: Each Item's landmark carries a popover template with its label, description, and note (an implementation callout adds its body; review slides list it under Surprises). Unselected noted elements get hidden note targets.
item.label: Inert templates beside landmarks

item.description: Measures noted elements as it does Item elements, adds focusable note hotspots, and drives the popover on hover, focus, tap, Tab, and Escape; an implementation Item's code drawer heads its code with the note.
item.label: Hotspots for noted elements

item.body: You might expect only noted elements to change; every Item hotspot now shows its label and description on hover, so existing decks gain previews too.
item.description: Why existing decks change even without notes.
item.label: Every Item hotspot now previews

item.description: One fixed popover, on the first side of the hotspot that covers no other hotspot. Opened by hover it lets the pointer through; a tap, click, or keyboard focus pins it for its links.
item.label: One popover that never blocks

item.description: A tampered source reaches the page only sanitized. The browser test hovers, tabs through a note's links, taps, dismisses, clicks an Item beneath a note and beside a surprise badge, and reads a drawer's note.
item.label: Server and browser tests

item.description: A callout renders as a warning badge at its element's bottom-left. When another Item explains the same element, the callout lets clicks through, so that Item's code stays reachable.
item.label: Surprises get their own badge

slide.takeaway: The server renders each note into an inert template; the page script measures a copy of the SVG and shows one popover beside the hotspot.
slide.title: The popover lives on the page, not in the frame
